verdict.rationale: Calendly documents scopes that "control which Calendly resources your integration can read or modify". It also documents several ways to issue credentials: personal access tokens for internal apps, per-user OAuth 2.1 tokens via PKCE, and Dynamic Client Registration so MCP-connected agents get their own OAuth client. Together these provide scoped, least-privilege credentials an agent can use. missing for 10: detail on how granular the scopes are, confirmation that personal access tokens can be scoped (not just OAuth apps), and independent or hands-on corroboration of least-privilege agent setups.
